## PLAN REVIEW PASSED (0 blocking, 1 advisory) — attestation certified. **CLAIMABLE NOW.**

This is the **only story in epic e369 that can be worked in parallel right now.** Every other child fast-fails `review-plan` as `INDETERMINATE` until its prerequisites close; J5 has no unclosed prerequisite.

Its earlier `stale-code` drift (a `Makefile` dependency change) was cleared by the fresh review.

To pick it up: `rebar claim c97f-90ae-4976-47c7 --assignee <you>` — note the **parent-first cascade** is already satisfied, since epic `e369` is claimed and `in_progress`.

Suggested worktree: reuse `/Users/joeoakhart/rebar-jira-family` (branch `jira-family-seam`, own `.venv` with an editable rebar-HEAD install) **or** cut a fresh one from `origin/main`. Either way prefix commands with `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH"` so the pre-commit hook finds ruff/mypy.

One consistency note from the epic's plan review: the epic body now names this story's exact image and rationale — `pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1` at `http://localhost:2990/jira`, chosen because 8.17.1 is >= 8.14 (the release that introduced PATs), with the version-drift limitation tracked at `9895-ac7d-4276-4f08`. That matches this story; no change needed here.

Also relevant to your implementation: the epic now **requires `https` for the DC `base_url` unless `allow_insecure = true`**. Because this harness serves plain HTTP on loopback, the live tests that consume it (J6/J7) must set `allow_insecure = true` explicitly and assert the warning fires — the harness is the *intended* override case, not a bypass.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
OPERATIONAL FINDINGS from actually building and running the harness on this host (recorded during execution; some contradict assumptions in the plan text).

1. THE IMAGE DOES NOT CONTAIN JIRA. 'atlas-run' downloads Jira 8.17.1 from maven.atlassian.com AT RUNTIME on first start. Verified in the container log: 'Configured Artifact: com.atlassian.jira.plugins:jira-plugin-test-resources:8.17.1:zip' followed by a stream of 'Downloading from atlassian-public: https://maven.atlassian.com/repository/public/...'. Consequences the harness design must account for:
   * NETWORK EGRESS to maven.atlassian.com is a hard runtime dependency, not just a one-time image pull. An air-gapped or egress-restricted CI runner cannot start this harness at all.
   * First start is dominated by that download, so the readiness timeout must cover a large artifact fetch, not just JVM boot.
   * Mounting a persistent Maven cache (~/.m2) as a volume should make repeat starts dramatically faster; without it every fresh container re-downloads.
   * SUPPLY-CHAIN/LONGEVITY RISK: if Atlassian ever withdraws the 8.17.1 artifacts from their public Maven repo, the harness stops working even though our Dockerfile digest is pinned. Pinning the base image does NOT pin Jira itself. That is worth stating in the README as the real fragility, and it strengthens the case for the separately-tracked real-instance validation (9895-ac7d-4276-4f08).

2. THE 'CARRIES ITS OWN LICENSE' CLAIM IS UNVERIFIED AND SHOULD NOT BE ASSERTED. What is actually true and observed: no license key had to be supplied to build or start it; the Atlassian SDK's atlas-run provisions the instance itself. Whether that constitutes a bundled license is a legal characterization I have not verified, so the README should describe the observed behavior ('no license key is supplied; the SDK provisions a local developer instance') rather than making a licensing claim.

3. EMULATION IS SEVERE HERE, not a minor tax. Base is linux/amd64; this host is arm64. Upstream README quotes 'first responsive request typically within ~3-5 minutes'. At 10+ minutes on this host the instance was still in the Maven download phase with REST not yet answering. So the plan's readiness timeout must be generous by default AND the README should say a native-amd64 runner is strongly preferred, not merely nicer.

Still measuring whether it comes up at all on emulated arm64; that result decides whether this story is verifiable on THIS host or whether its acceptance evidence must come from an amd64 runner. Recording the finding either way rather than assuming success.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
HARNESS RUN #1 FAILED ON THIS HOST — definitive, with the exact cause. Recording because it changes what this story can promise and where its acceptance evidence can come from.

WHAT HAPPENED: the container ran ~25 minutes and then EXITED 1. It was NOT a config error and NOT a download failure. Jira really did come down and start booting — the log confirms 'JIRA Build : 8.17.1#817001-sha1:36e93c711dfb14e6e1509a2fef6b04c4d73cc7ca', Tomcat 8x started, H2 configured, plugin system starting. The fatal line is:
  DeployerWatchdog: Deployable [http://localhost:2990/cargocpc/index.html] failed to finish deploying within the timeout period [600000]
  ERROR Failed to execute goal com.atlassian.maven.plugins:jira-maven-plugin:8.0.2:run: Cannot start container [Tomcat8xInstalledLocalContainer]
So **Cargo's deploy watchdog has a hardcoded-by-default 600000 ms (10 minute) ceiling, and Jira cannot finish booting inside it under arm64 emulation.** The upstream README's '~3-5 minutes' is a native-amd64 figure; emulated, boot exceeds 10 minutes and Cargo kills it.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THIS HOST: the 600s ceiling is a property of the harness, not of my laptop. Any slow or contended runner — an emulated arch, a throttled CI box, a cold Maven cache competing for I/O — hits the same wall. A readiness probe with a generous timeout does NOT help, because the container is dead before the probe could ever succeed: the failure is INSIDE the container's own startup, not in our polling. That is a distinction the plan had wrong by implication.

MITIGATION UNDER TEST (not asserted): rebuilt with the entrypoint raised to
  ENTRYPOINT ["atlas-run", "-DskipAllPrompts=true", "-DstartupTimeout=2700000", "-Dcargo.timeout=2700000"]
and started it on :2991 with a PERSISTENT Maven volume (jira-m2-cache) so the ~917-artifact download is not repeated. Measuring now. I am deliberately not claiming the flags work until observed — the point of this story is a harness that provably starts, so an unverified flag would be exactly the kind of assumption the epic exists to eliminate.

REGARDLESS OF THE OUTCOME, the plan must state: (a) the Cargo startup-timeout override belongs in the vendored Dockerfile with this failure recorded as the reason, or a maintainer will 'clean up' the flag and reintroduce a 25-minute silent death; (b) a native-amd64 runner is a REQUIREMENT for practical use, not a preference; and (c) acceptance evidence for this story must name the architecture it was produced on.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
HARNESS VERIFICATION ON THIS HOST: CONCLUSIVELY NOT POSSIBLE. Three runs, and the finding is firm enough to act on rather than keep burning time.

RUN 1 (plain upstream entrypoint): died at ~25 min. Cause: 'DeployerWatchdog: Deployable [http://localhost:2990/cargocpc/index.html] failed to finish deploying within the timeout period [600000]' -> 'Cannot start container [Tomcat8xInstalledLocalContainer]'. Jira genuinely booted (JIRA Build 8.17.1#817001-sha1:36e93c711dfb...) and reached 'Starting the JIRA Plugin System'; Cargo's 10-minute deploy ceiling killed it.
RUN 2 (-DstartupTimeout / -Dcargo.timeout): died the SAME way, still 'timeout period [600000]'. Those two property names have NO effect on the AMPS/jira-maven-plugin run goal. My guess was wrong and I am recording it as wrong.
RUN 3 (-Dproduct.start.timeout=2700000, found in Atlassian's own docs, not guessed): ran 55 MINUTES with NO DeployerWatchdog kill at all — so **-Dproduct.start.timeout IS the correct knob** and the 600s ceiling is genuinely overridable. But it never reached 'Starting the JIRA Plugin System' (grep count 0); it was still crawling in the plugin's own surefire phase at 55 min. Emulation, not configuration, is the wall.

NET FOR WHOEVER IMPLEMENTS THIS:
 * USE -Dproduct.start.timeout in the vendored Dockerfile's ENTRYPOINT. This is now empirically established, and it must carry a comment citing run 1's failure, or a maintainer will drop it and reintroduce a silent ~25-minute death that reads like a network fault.
 * -DstartupTimeout and -Dcargo.timeout are NOT the property names. Recorded so nobody repeats my two wasted runs.
 * A NATIVE amd64 RUNNER IS A HARD REQUIREMENT, not a preference. On emulated arm64 the instance does not become usable within an hour even with the timeout lifted.
 * ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE FOR THIS STORY MUST NAME THE ARCHITECTURE IT WAS PRODUCED ON. Mine would have been produced on arm64 and is therefore unavailable; that is a fact about this host, not a defect in the plan.

ENVIRONMENT LEFT CLEAN: removed all three probe containers and the Maven cache volume, and deleted my two throwaway images. Kept ONLY 'pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1' (879MB) — the canonical upstream-named build — so a later amd64 attempt does not re-download ~900 Maven artifacts. Delete it with 'docker rmi pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1' if the space is wanted.

STATUS: this story remains OPEN and UNCLAIMED. I am not claiming a ticket whose acceptance criteria (AC1: the readiness probe reports REST answering; AC2: a smoke test creates and reads back an issue) cannot be satisfied on the available hardware. Claiming it to author files I cannot verify would put unproven work behind a green-looking board.

comments.body:
CANARY-PRECISION FINDING — my plan said 'the pre-existing job is left alone'. That is safe but SUBTLY WRONG, and I am correcting it in implementation.
MEASURED, not assumed. tests/external/conftest.py's canary predicate is _jira_canary_should_fail(collected, executed) == 'collected >= 1 and executed == 0' — a GLOBAL count over every jira_live-marked item in the session, not a per-directory one. And the pre-existing 'external' job runs 'pytest -m external tests/external -q' over the WHOLE tree with REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1 plus live CLOUD Jira creds, but no DC harness.
CONSEQUENCE: my 4 new DC tests get collected there, skip (nothing at localhost:2990), and are counted as jira_live. Because the existing Cloud live tests DO execute, executed > 0, so the canary does NOT fail — no breakage. But the DC tests' all-skip is now MASKED by the Cloud tests. The canary silently loses the ability to detect 'every DC test skipped', which is precisely the condition it exists to catch. That is a real, if quiet, weakening of an existing guard.
I verified BOTH branches locally before concluding: with no opt-in -> 4 skipped, canary silent. With REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1 and no harness -> 4 skipped AND '[jira-live-canary] FAIL: ... collected=4 executed=0 ... validated nothing'. So the sentinel wiring and the canary both work; the masking is purely an artifact of sharing one session with the Cloud tests.
FIX (small, surgical): add '--ignore=tests/external/live_jira_dc' to the pre-existing job's pytest invocation, so the two tiers stay independent and EACH job's canary means what it says — the Cloud job's canary covers Cloud, the new DC job's canary covers DC. This is a one-flag change to a working job, chosen over the alternative of leaving the guard degraded.
Recorded here rather than silently edited into the plan, because it contradicts a sentence the plan currently asserts.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
FIRST LIVE RUN ON NATIVE AMD64 — THE HARNESS WORKS. GitHub Actions run 30507727332, job 'jira DC harness smoke', on merged commit a20ccd89b.
STEP-BY-STEP, this is the vindication of the whole build-not-pull + amd64 diagnosis:
  Build and start the Jira DC harness .......... SUCCESS
  Wait for Jira DC to become ready ............. SUCCESS
  Run the Jira DC harness smoke tests .......... failure (3 passed, 1 error)
  Tear down .................................... SUCCESS
The instance BUILT from the vendored Dockerfile, BOOTED, and ANSWERED REST — in about 7 minutes wall-clock for the whole job, against three local attempts that never got there in 25-55 minutes. Native amd64 was exactly the missing ingredient, and Cargo's 600000ms ceiling never fired.
WHAT THE 3 PASSING TESTS PROVE (these are the substantive ones):
 * test_instance_is_a_server_deployment_at_the_pinned_version — it really is Jira 8.x with deploymentType != Cloud, so DC's REST v2 semantics are what we are exercising, not Cloud's v3+ADF.
 * test_personal_access_token_authenticates_via_bearer — PAT BEARER AUTH WORKS against a real 8.17.1, minted programmatically via POST /rest/pat/latest/tokens. That is the DC auth mode J6's transport will use, now proven rather than assumed.
 * test_a_bogus_bearer_token_is_rejected — the contrast case, so the PAT result is not an artifact of the endpoint accepting anything.
THE ONE FAILURE was MY fixture, not the harness: it hardcoded projectTemplateKey 'com.pyxis.greenhopper.jira:gh-simplified-kanban-classic' — a plausible, widely-cited Software template — and the instance replied '400 The project template specified does not exist'.
FIX (change 1019): I did NOT substitute another guess. That would be the third time in this story I guessed an identifier and was wrong (pullable image name; -DstartupTimeout/-Dcargo.timeout). The instance is the only authority on which templates it has, so the fixture now DISCOVERS them via GET /rest/project-templates/latest/templates and tries each in turn, then a bare software project, then a bare project, taking the first 201. On total failure it reports EVERY attempt with its status instead of a lone 400, so a future image bump says what it tried.
ALSO CAUGHT DURING THE EDIT: my insertion left the original '@pytest.fixture' decorator attached to the new _discover_project_templates helper, which would have made a plain helper into a fixture and broken it when called directly. Found by checking decorator placement with an AST walk after the edit rather than trusting that a clean 'ruff check' and a successful collect meant the structure was right — neither would have caught it.
J5 remains IN_PROGRESS. Its ACs require the smoke tests to actually pass; 3 of 4 is not done.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
FRESHNESS AC NOW IMPLEMENTED (change 1026) — the completion verifier was right that only half of it existed.
WHAT WAS MISSING: the AC has two halves. 'make jira-dc-up brings up a FRESH instance (--force-recreate' was satisfied at Makefile:181. 'and the fixture refuses to run against a container it did not start into a known-clean state' was NOT implemented anywhere — the session fixture only waited for readiness. The verifier read the code correctly; I had shipped the easy half.
WHY I DID NOT IMPLEMENT IT LITERALLY: proving the container's PROVENANCE ('did I start this one?') is not observable after the fact — --force-recreate leaves no durable marker a later pytest session can read, and a container label would only prove which compose invocation created it, not that its Jira is clean. So I asserted the property the AC actually exists to protect: NO RESIDUE FROM A PRIOR RUN IS PRESENT. That is strictly stronger for the stated risk ('an interrupted previous teardown cannot leak stale Jira state into the next run'), because it also catches a freshly-created container that some other process has since dirtied.
MECHANISM: every scratch project is keyed RBJ + 4 letters and a completed run deletes its own, so any RBJ-prefixed project present at session start is residue. Found via /rest/api/2/project — the DIRECT project list, never the search index, same ADR 0037 discipline as teardown, since a lagging index could equally hide real residue or invent phantom residue. On residue the session fixture raises with the exact recovery command (make jira-dc-down && make jira-dc-up) rather than testing against dirty state.
PROVEN, not assumed — the guard cannot be exercised by the live suite without deliberately dirtying a real instance, so I unit-checked its discriminator directly against a mocked project list:
  clean instance          [DEMO, TEST]                -> []            OK
  residue present         [DEMO, RBJABCD]             -> [RBJABCD]     OK
  multiple residue        [RBJZZZZ, RBJAAAA]          -> sorted pair   OK
  LOOKALIKES not residue  [RB, RBX, ARBJ1]            -> []            OK  (prefix must not over-match)
  unreadable project list (503)                       -> []            OK  (must not INVENT residue and block a good run)
The lookalike and the unreadable cases are the two ways this guard could have been worse than useless — over-matching would block every run, and inventing residue on a transient 5xx would make the harness flaky. Both pinned.
Pushed as change 1026.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
RE-VERIFIED GREEN WITH THE FRESHNESS GUARD IN PLACE. Run https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/30515632763 on merged commit bb951f6e4, ubuntu-latest (native x86_64). Every step SUCCESS; '4 passed in 6.39s'; teardown clean; the failure-logs step skipped because nothing failed.
WHY I RE-RAN RATHER THAN REUSING THE EARLIER GREEN: the guard added in change 1026 executes in the SESSION FIXTURE, before any test. If it over-matched a prefix or tripped on a transient project-list read it would block the entire suite — and the previous green run could not have covered code that did not exist yet. A prior pass is not evidence for code added after it.
READINESS DATA POINT WORTH KEEPING: 'Jira DC ready after 96 tries' = ~8 minutes at the 5s cadence, against 37 tries (~3 min) on the previous run. Same image, same runner class. That ~2.7x spread across consecutive runs is exactly why the 20-minute default budget is not padding — a 5-minute default would have failed this run while the harness was working correctly. Recorded so nobody 'optimizes' the timeout down using a single fast observation.
ALL FOUR SMOKE TESTS PASS against a real Jira 8.17.1 Server: the REST v2 create/read round trip (asserting round-tripped VALUES and that description returns a plain string, i.e. v2/wiki not v3/ADF), PAT bearer auth with a programmatically minted token, the bogus-token contrast case, and the serverInfo deployment/version assertion. Teardown is index-independent throughout.
J5's acceptance evidence is complete.

compiled_state.description:
# J5 — A Dockerized Jira harness as the Data Center verification oracle

## Context / Problem

There is no way to buy a Jira Data Center license to test against: Atlassian ended new DC purchases on
30 March 2026 and no longer issues DC trial licenses. There is also **no official OpenAPI/Swagger spec for Jira
DC** — Atlassian publishes only WADL, and the long-standing requests for one (JRASERVER-65954, JRASERVER-68539)
remain open — so spec-driven contract testing is unavailable. Cloud's v3 swagger is not a substitute: different
auth, ADF vs wiki markup, accountId vs name. Without an oracle, a DC adapter is unverifiable except against
fakes that encode our own assumptions.

## Approach

Use the **purpose-built test image the pycontribs/jira project uses for exactly this problem** — a thin wrapper
over `addono/jira-software-standalone` that stands up a real Jira 8.17.1 at `http://localhost:2990/jira` with
default credentials `admin`/`admin`. It is unaffected by the DC trial shutdown, and it is the substrate the most
widely used Python Jira client validates itself against. Jira 8.17.1 is **≥ 8.14**, the release that introduced
Personal Access Tokens, so the PAT bearer auth the DC transport uses is exercised for real.

**The image must be BUILT, not pulled — corrected against the registry, not assumed.** An earlier draft of this
plan said to `docker run pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1` and called it "a pinned, pullable image". That is
false and was verified false before this plan was rewritten:

- `docker pull pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1` → `pull access denied ... repository does not exist`.
- The Docker Hub API for `pycontribs/jira-test-image` returns `{"message": "object not found"}`. The
  `pycontribs` Hub namespace contains exactly seven repositories, all OS base images (centos, fedora, ubuntu,
  debian, alpine, opensuse, voidlinux). There is no `jira-test-image`.
- That tag is a **local build name**. `pycontribs/jira` carries `docker/jira-test-image/{Dockerfile,README.md}`,
  and the upstream README's own instruction is
  `docker build -t pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1 docker/jira-test-image`. It is published to no registry.
- Its base, `addono/jira-software-standalone`, **is** pullable, and the exact digest pycontribs pins
  (`sha256:04326628dc4ac36b2bfc1d0f2ebe5ba3807c1ec9cf9b18307d3c2ad7222537e9`) resolves.

Feasibility was proven before this rewrite: the upstream Dockerfile was fetched and built on the target host
(879 MB image, container starts and stays up). So the oracle is real; only the acquisition mechanism changes.

**Decision: vendor a ~15-line Dockerfile in `tests/external/live_jira_dc/`** that `FROM`s the addono base **by digest**
and reproduces the two things the upstream wrapper adds, with attribution to pycontribs/jira in a comment.
Rationale: building from a third-party repo at test time would make the harness depend on another project's
directory layout and default branch staying put; vendoring the few lines is self-documenting and pins our own
supply chain. The alternative — a `git clone` of pycontribs/jira in the fixture — is rejected for that reason.

**Three details are load-bearing and must survive into the vendored file as comments**, because each looks like
removable noise and each breaks the harness if removed:

1. **`-DskipAllPrompts=true` on the `atlas-run` ENTRYPOINT is MANDATORY.** Atlassian shut down the Marketplace
   v1 REST endpoint that AMPS hardcodes for its SDK update check, so without this flag **every cold container
   start** fails with `FileNotFoundException` on `https://marketplace.atlassian.com/rest/1.0/plugins/...`. The
   failure looks like a transient network fault, so a maintainer "tidying" the flag away would produce a
   confusing, seemingly-flaky breakage.
2. **`-dit` (equivalently compose's `tty: true` + `stdin_open: true`) is REQUIRED** — AMPS exits without a
   controlling TTY. A plain compose service block is not sufficient.
3. **Only Jira 8.x is supported.** `JIRA_VERSION` is overridable across 8.x patch versions, but 9+/11+ fail
   Maven resolution because the upstream pom is anchored to the 8.x dependency graph. The README must say so,
   or a future reader will assume the harness can track a client's newer Jira by bumping a variable.

**The image does NOT contain Jira — `atlas-run` downloads it at runtime.** Verified by running it: the
container log shows `Configured Artifact: com.atlassian.jira.plugins:jira-plugin-test-resources:8.17.1:zip`
followed by ~917 `Downloading from atlassian-public: https://maven.atlassian.com/...` lines before Tomcat and
H2 come up. Four consequences the harness must design around:

- **Egress to `maven.atlassian.com` is a hard RUNTIME dependency**, not a one-time image pull. An
  egress-restricted CI runner cannot start this harness at all.
- **`pinning the image digest does NOT pin Jira itself`.** If Atlassian withdraws the 8.17.1 artifacts from
  their public Maven repo, the harness stops working despite our pinned base digest. That, not the image, is
  the real fragility, and the README must say so — it also strengthens the case for the separately-tracked
  real-instance validation (`9895-ac7d-4276-4f08`).
- First start is dominated by that download, so the readiness budget must cover a large artifact fetch, not
  just JVM boot.
- The fixture SHOULD mount a persistent Maven cache (`~/.m2`) as a volume, or every fresh container
  re-downloads ~900 artifacts.

**No licensing claim is made.** An earlier draft said the image "carries its own license". That is a legal
characterization this story has not verified, so it is replaced by the observed behaviour: no license key is
supplied to build or start the instance, and the Atlassian SDK's `atlas-run` provisions a local developer
instance. The README states it that way.

**Local runs on Apple Silicon are the constrained path, and were measured.** Three attempts on an arm64
workstation failed: two killed by Cargo's default 600000 ms deploy ceiling, and a third — with
`-Dproduct.start.timeout` correctly lifting that ceiling — still never reached Jira startup in 55 minutes. Two
compounding causes, both recorded so a future reader does not repeat the runs: (a) the amd64 base under arm64
**emulation**, and (b) **resource starvation** — the colima VM was 2 vCPU / 4 GiB with seven other containers
already resident, against a Jira that wants ~2 GB of heap by itself. A local run therefore needs BOTH a larger,
Rosetta-backed VM (e.g. `colima start --cpu 6 --memory 12 --vm-type vz --vz-rosetta`) AND spare capacity; since
that restarts the VM and evicts every running container, it is an operator decision, not something the harness
can assume. Prefer the CI job.

**Platform is a real variable, not a footnote.** The base image is `linux/amd64`. On an `arm64` host (Apple
Silicon, ARM CI runners) it runs under emulation, and the upstream README's "first responsive request within
~3-5 minutes" does not hold — observed startup on an emulated arm64 host is materially slower. So the compose
file sets `platform: linux/amd64` **explicitly** (making behaviour deterministic instead of dependent on the
host's default resolution), and the readiness probe's timeout is generous and overridable by env var rather
than a hardcoded few minutes. The README records that a native-amd64 runner is strongly preferred.

**Stated limitation, deliberately accepted:** 8.17.1 is older than the version a client such as CMS is likely
running, so this harness proves REST v2 protocol semantics, not deployment-specific behavior (workflow names,
custom fields, permission schemes, user directories). Closing that gap requires access to the real instance and
is tracked separately as ticket `9895-ac7d-4276-4f08`; this story's README records the exact image tag so that
comparison has a baseline.

Add the harness under **`tests/external/live_jira_dc/`** with a compose file, a readiness probe that polls until
the instance answers REST, and a fixture that provisions a scratch project and tears down everything it created.

**The tier is `external`, NOT `integration` — corrected against the CI workflow.** An earlier draft marked these
`integration`, reasoning that `make test` runs `pytest -m "not integration and not external"`
(**`Makefile:178`** — verified; an earlier draft cited 154, which is inside the `actionlint-bin` recipe) and so
would exclude them. That reasoning is wrong, and dangerously so: `_build-and-test.yml` runs
**`pytest -m integration` as its own dedicated CI step on every commit** ("Run the integration tier
(concurrency + reconciler; network-guarded)"), explicitly because those tests "need no live services (mocked
acli / local git)". So the `integration` marker is an **INCLUSION into CI**, not an exclusion — Docker-requiring
tests marked that way would be collected and run on every commit against a runner with no container, no Jira
and no egress, breaking CI for everyone.

The `external` tier is the one genuinely fenced off, and it is enforced structurally rather than by convention:
`tests/conftest.py::pytest_collection_modifyitems` (a) **auto-applies** the `external` marker to every item
under `tests/external/`, so no per-file marker is needed, and (b) **hard-fails collection** if any item carries
`external` while living outside `tests/external/` — so a live test cannot hide elsewhere in the tree.
`external` runs only from `external-integration.yml` (`workflow_dispatch` + a weekly cron), never on a commit.
Living under `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` therefore satisfies the gating requirement AND supplies the
structural backstop for free.

**Living under `tests/external/` means INHERITING that tier's contract — three mechanisms, all enumerated
here because each silently changes how this suite behaves:**

1. **`_require_external_opt_in` (autouse, `tests/external/conftest.py`) SKIPS every test under
   `tests/external/` unless `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1`.** It is a deliberate leak-guard (bug
   `4a48-6dd5-aef3-4c8e`): external tests must stay inert on a default invocation even when credentials happen
   to be present. Consequence for this story: `make jira-dc-up && pytest tests/external/live_jira_dc/` **skips
   everything** without the env var. The README must lead with the full invocation, and the readiness probe's
   error message is only reachable in an opted-in run.
2. **The `_live_jira_ready` sentinel drives the `jira_live` auto-marker and the all-skip canary.**
   `tests/external/conftest.py::pytest_collection_modifyitems` applies `jira_live` to any module defining a
   module-level `_live_jira_ready`, and `pytest_sessionfinish` **fails the session** when at least one
   `jira_live` test was collected but none executed — the guard against a scheduled run that validated nothing.
   Every existing live-Jira module defines it (`test_reconcile_live.py`, `test_link_sync_live.py`,
   `test_link_sync_roundtrip_live.py`, `test_verified_fake_contract_live.py`). **`test_harness_smoke.py` MUST
   define `_live_jira_ready` too**, or it opts out of the canary and a silently-all-skipped harness run would
   look green.
3. **`_allow_live_model_requests`** re-enables pydantic-ai's global kill-switch for this tier. Irrelevant to
   this harness (it makes no model calls) but noted so the inherited fixture set is fully accounted for.

**Skip-vs-fail is settled here, because the tier forces it.** An earlier draft's "failure path" said the suite
should FAIL with a "harness not running" message when the instance is down. That is wrong for this tier and
would break the existing `external-integration.yml` job, which already runs `pytest -m external tests/external`
with no Docker anywhere. The correct contract: **absent harness ⇒ SKIP with a clear, actionable message**
(naming `make jira-dc-up` and `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1`), and the **canary** — not a hard failure — is what
prevents a vacuous green, because a run that collected `jira_live` tests and executed none fails the session.
That gives both properties: no CI breakage when Docker is absent, and no silent nothing-ran success.

Teardown follows **`docs/adr/0037-reconciler-live-validation-harness.md` §3** (named in full because FIVE ADRs
share the `0037-` prefix — code-review-novelty-convergence, cross-ticket-overlap, oss-contribution-intake-posture,
reconciler-live-validation-harness, transport-retry — so a bare "ADR 0037" is unresolvable), which
**prohibits post-deletion search-index assertions** because Jira's index
lags creates and deletes by an unbounded interval and can return stale results either way. So the teardown
oracle is not "query the project and find it empty": it asserts each delete call's HTTP status and then polls
each issue's **direct REST endpoint** (`/rest/api/2/issue/{key}`) until it returns 404, which is index-independent.

**Alternative rejected: fixtures and a stateful fake alone.** rebar's test-design standard allows a verified
fake for external-service mapping, but a fake verified only against fixtures we recorded cannot falsify
assumptions we never thought to record — transitions, permission errors, link direction. The fake is still
built (J6 uses it for fast unit tests); this story gives it something real to be verified against.

**Alternative rejected: reusing pycontribs/jira's test assertions as the oracle.** Their tests assert their
client's behavior, not rebar's field mapping. The reusable asset is the image and harness pattern, which is
what this story takes.

**Alternative rejected: the Atlassian SDK's `atlas-run-standalone`.** It also yields a licensed local Jira, but
it needs the full SDK toolchain and its licenses are short-lived (3-day timebombs requiring `atlas-mvn clean`
recycling), which is hostile to repeatable CI. A pinned Docker image has neither problem.

## Scope

- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/Dockerfile` (new) — the vendored wrapper: `FROM` the addono base **by digest**, the
  `-DskipAllPrompts=true` entrypoint, and the three rationale comments above plus attribution to
  pycontribs/jira.
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/docker-compose.yml`, `conftest.py`, `README.md` (new) — compose `build`s the local
  Dockerfile (it does NOT reference an unpullable image), sets `platform: linux/amd64`, `tty: true`,
  `stdin_open: true`, mounts a persistent Maven cache volume, and publishes
  **`127.0.0.1:2990:2990`** — loopback-scoped, NOT the bare `2990:2990` an earlier draft said, which Docker
  binds on `0.0.0.0` and would expose a well-known-`admin`/`admin` Jira to the whole network.
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_harness_smoke.py` (new).
- **`.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` — a NEW, SEPARATE job, modelled on the `langfuse-trace` job
  that already exists in this same file.** This is the key practical finding: the workflow ALREADY implements
  this exact shape at lines ~159-251 for an ephemeral self-hosted Langfuse — `docker compose ... up -d`, poll
  until healthy with an `::error::` + `logs --tail` on timeout, run the tests, dump logs `if: failure()`, and
  `docker compose ... down -v` under `if: always()`. So the Jira job is a direct adaptation of a working
  in-repo precedent rather than novel CI engineering; copy its structure and swap the compose file, the health
  URL (`/jira/rest/api/2/serverInfo`) and the test path.

  **`ubuntu-latest` resolves the platform problem entirely.** GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` runners are native
  **x86_64**, so the amd64 base image runs WITHOUT emulation — which was the sole reason this harness could not
  be verified on an Apple-Silicon workstation. rebar is a PUBLIC repo, so the standard runner is 4 vCPU /
  16 GB, comfortably above Jira 8.17.1's needs. And because this workflow triggers only on
  `workflow_dispatch` + a weekly cron, a 10-20 minute harness never touches per-commit CI.
  **CI — specifically a new job in this workflow — is therefore the PRIMARY intended home for this harness's
  acceptance evidence**, and a local run is the optional convenience path, not the reverse. This workflow is an unenumerated
  consumer in earlier drafts: at line 141 it already runs `pytest -m external tests/external -q`, so the new
  directory is collected by it the moment the files land, and it has **no** docker build/up/down steps. It also
  gates its existing job on an LLM API key, which this harness does not need. So the harness gets its **own
  job** (not an extension of the LLM-keyed one) that: builds the vendored Dockerfile, brings the instance up,
  waits on the readiness probe, runs ONLY `tests/external/live_jira_dc/`, and tears down in an `if: always()`
  step. It must run on a **native amd64 runner** (see the platform note above). The pre-existing job is left
  alone, and because the harness tests skip cleanly without `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1` plus a reachable instance,
  its collection of them stays harmless.
- `Makefile` — a `jira-dc-up` target only; the `test:` target is NOT modified (the `integration` marker is
  already excluded by its existing `-m` expression at **`Makefile:178`**), and `jira-dc-up` is added to the
  `.PHONY` list at `Makefile:30` — without that, a file or directory named `jira-dc-up` would make the target
  silently no-op.

## Testing

Real-external-service tier by construction — this story *is* the harness. Its own oracle is that the harness
starts, is usable, and provably cleans up.

- happy path: the harness starts, the readiness probe reports REST answering, and a smoke test creates and
  reads back one issue through raw REST v2.
- auth path: a Personal Access Token minted on the 8.17.1 instance authenticates a request via
  `Authorization: Bearer`, proving the DC auth mode the transport will use is exercised, not assumed.
- teardown oracle (index-independent, per ADR 0037 §3): after a deliberately failing test, every issue the
  fixture created returns 404 from its direct `/rest/api/2/issue/{key}` endpoint, and each delete call's HTTP
  status was 2xx. Search is never consulted.
- gating oracle: `pytest --collect-only -m "not integration and not external"` collects zero tests from
  `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` — and, separately, the `external` marker is auto-applied by
  `tests/external/conftest.py` rather than written per-file, with misplacement hard-failing collection.
- canary participation: `test_harness_smoke.py` defines `_live_jira_ready`, so its tests carry `jira_live` and
  an opted-in run in which every one of them skipped **fails the session** instead of reporting a vacuous pass.
- failure path (absent harness): with the instance down, the suite **SKIPS** with a message naming
  `make jira-dc-up` and `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1` — not a raw connection traceback, and not a hard failure, which
  would break the pre-existing `external` CI job that has no Docker.

**The `allow_insecure` obligation is NOT this story's — it belongs to J6/J7.** A draft of this plan added an AC
requiring every live test here to set `allow_insecure = true` and assert the cleartext warning. That was wrong
on two counts, recorded so nobody restores it: (a) the `allow_insecure` config key and its warning-emitting
validator DO NOT EXIST yet — they are **J6's** deliverable ([rebar:9fd4-a94c-156e-4a56], which already carries
exactly that AC), so J5 could not satisfy it while J6 is open, contradicting this story's whole point of being
independently claimable; and (b) it does not even apply here — J5's smoke tests speak **raw REST v2** to the
instance and never construct rebar's DC backend or read rebar's config, so no validator is on their path. The
epic's step-7 obligation attaches to the stories whose live tests drive rebar's DC transport against this
harness (J6/J7), which is where it is already recorded.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] the harness **builds from the vendored `tests/external/live_jira_dc/Dockerfile`** and starts (via the compose
      file or the `jira-dc-up` target), and the readiness probe reports REST v2 answering at
      `http://localhost:2990/jira`. The criterion is explicitly BUILD-and-start, not pull-and-start: no
      acceptance step may depend on `pycontribs/jira-test-image` being pullable, because it is not published
- [ ] the vendored `Dockerfile` pins the addono base **by digest** (not by tag), keeps
      `-DskipAllPrompts=true` on the `atlas-run` entrypoint, and carries a comment explaining that removing
      that flag breaks every cold start via the retired Marketplace v1 endpoint
- [ ] the compose service sets `platform: linux/amd64`, `tty: true` and `stdin_open: true`, and the readiness
      timeout is env-overridable — so an emulated arm64 host is slow rather than spuriously failing
- [ ] a smoke test creates and reads back an issue via REST v2, and a PAT-authenticated request succeeds
- [ ] `test_harness_smoke.py` defines a module-level `_live_jira_ready` sentinel, so its tests receive the
      `jira_live` marker from `tests/external/conftest.py` and participate in the all-skip canary — an opted-in
      run where every harness test skipped must FAIL the session rather than report a vacuous pass
- [ ] with no instance running, the suite SKIPS with a message naming BOTH `make jira-dc-up` and
      `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1` (the tier's autouse opt-in guard), and does NOT fail — verified by running the
      directory with the harness down, which must not break the pre-existing `external` CI job
- [ ] `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` gains a SEPARATE amd64 job that builds the Dockerfile,
      waits on the readiness probe, runs only `tests/external/live_jira_dc/`, and tears down under
      `if: always()`. The pre-existing LLM-keyed job keeps its steps, secrets and gating untouched with
      exactly ONE deliberate exception: `--ignore=tests/external/live_jira_dc` is added to its pytest
      invocation. That exception is required and was decided during execution (recorded in this ticket's
      comments): `tests/external/conftest.py`'s all-skip canary counts `jira_live` items GLOBALLY, and that
      job runs `pytest -m external tests/external` over the whole tree with live Cloud creds. Without the
      flag the DC tests are collected there, skip for want of a harness, and their all-skip is MASKED by the
      Cloud tests that do execute — silently costing the canary its ability to detect "every DC test
      skipped", the exact condition it exists to catch. The flag keeps each job's canary meaningful for its
      own tier. An earlier draft of this AC asserted the job was wholly unmodified; that is corrected here
      rather than left contradicting the code
- [ ] the vendored Dockerfile's entrypoint carries **`-Dproduct.start.timeout`** (empirically the correct AMPS
      property — `-DstartupTimeout` and `-Dcargo.timeout` were verified to have NO effect) with a comment citing
      the failure it prevents: without it Cargo's default 600000 ms deploy ceiling kills the container ~25
      minutes in with `Deployable [...] failed to finish deploying within the timeout period [600000]`, which
      reads like a network fault and invites a maintainer to delete the flag
- [ ] after an intentionally failing test run, every created issue returns 404 from its direct issue endpoint
      (no search query used anywhere in teardown verification)
- [ ] `pytest --collect-only -m "not integration and not external"` reports 0 tests collected from
      `tests/external/live_jira_dc/`, and `git diff Makefile` shows no change to the `test:` target
- [ ] the PAT is created **programmatically** by the fixture via `POST /rest/pat/latest/tokens` authenticated
      with the admin basic credentials (the Jira DC 8.14+ endpoint), and the resulting token is then used in an
      `Authorization: Bearer` request — so the auth AC is self-contained and does not depend on a
      hand-minted token
- [ ] the readiness probe has a **stated default timeout of 20 minutes** with a 5-second poll cadence,
      overridable by env var, and on expiry it fails with an explicit "harness not running / not ready" message
      naming the compose target — never a raw connection traceback. The generous default is deliberate: an
      emulated amd64 base plus a ~900-artifact Maven download makes upstream's quoted 3-5 minutes unattainable
      on an arm64 runner
- [ ] `jira-dc-up` brings up a **fresh** instance (`--force-recreate`, and the fixture refuses to run against a
      container it did not start into a known-clean state), so an interrupted previous teardown cannot leak
      stale Jira state into the next run
- [ ] the compose port binding is **loopback-scoped (`127.0.0.1:2990:2990`)**, not `0.0.0.0` — this instance has
      well-known `admin`/`admin` credentials and must not be reachable from other hosts on the network
- [ ] the structural backstop asserts the **ABSENCE of the `integration` marker**, not the presence of
      `external`. Naming the right marker is the whole point: `tests/external/conftest.py` auto-applies
      `external` to every item under `tests/external/` UNCONDITIONALLY, so a test asserting `external` is
      present would be **vacuously true and could never fail** — it would protect nothing. The real risk is a
      future file under `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` acquiring `integration` (via an explicit `pytestmark` or
      decorator), because `_build-and-test.yml` runs `pytest -m integration` as a dedicated per-commit step with
      no Docker available. So the test collects every item under that directory and asserts none carries
      `integration` — and a deliberately-marked scratch file must make it FAIL before being reverted, proving
      the assertion has teeth rather than being another tautology
- [ ] the feasibility evidence is **recorded reproducibly** in the README — the base digest, the resolved image
      size, the host architecture it was verified on, and the observed startup phases — rather than asserted as
      a one-off local success
- [ ] `tests/external/live_jira_dc/README.md` records the pinned base digest and Jira version, states the
      version-drift limitation naming ticket `9895-ac7d-4276-4f08` as where real-instance validation is
      tracked, AND records the two operational constraints a reader would otherwise rediscover the hard way:
      that only Jira 8.x works on this base (9+/11+ fail Maven resolution), and that the base is amd64 so an
      arm64 host emulates it and starts materially slower than the upstream's quoted 3-5 minutes
